data.title: AlUla Date Season Concludes with 'Al Shannah Day' to Highlight Agricultural Heritage
data.content:
AlUla, November 21, 2026, SPA -- The AlUla Date Season concludes today with “Al Shannah Day”, held at Al Manshiyah Farmers’ Market as part of the “Khairat AlUla” season. The event aims to highlight one of the traditional methods of preserving dates passed down through generations in AlUla, showcase the agricultural and cultural heritage associated with palm trees and dates, and pass knowledge and expertise on to future generations.
    The event highlights “Al Shannah”, a traditional means of preserving dates in AlUla. It is made from the hide of a sheep, lamb or goat, which is tanned, cleaned and prepared for use. The people of AlUla have long relied on Al Shannah to preserve dates and maintain their quality over extended periods, reflecting their inherited agricultural expertise in making use of local resources.
    The event offers residents and visitors an opportunity to learn about the stages of preserving dates using Al Shannah through live demonstrations by experienced members of the AlUla community. The process begins with sorting and cleaning the dates and preparing them for packing, followed by placing them inside Al Shannah and compressing them to minimize gaps, before stitching and sealing it tightly to protect the dates from air and moisture.
    Al Shannah is also closely associated with AlUla’s traditions of hospitality. Traditionally, the host would open it in front of a guest and serve dates as a gesture of generosity and welcome. Al Shannah is also used during the holy month of Ramadan. These customs have given it a significance beyond its practical role in preserving dates, making it part of the social memory associated with palm trees and dates, and a testament to the enduring relationship between people and agriculture in AlUla’s oases.
    In 2025, a total of 53 Al Shannah containers were sold at the World of Dates Exhibition, while the highest price paid for an old Al Shannah during that year’s Date Season reached SAR3,500. This reflects the continued presence of this heritage practice at agricultural and heritage events held in AlUla.
    Concluding the AlUla Date Season with “Al Shannah Day” is part of ongoing efforts to highlight the economic and cultural value of locally produced dates, preserve traditional agricultural practices and strengthen younger generations’ connection to the governorate’s agricultural heritage. The event takes place from 2 p.m. to 6 p.m. at Al Manshiyah Farmers’ Market.
    The AlUla Date Season is one of the agricultural seasons within “Khairat AlUla”, organised by the Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU). It forms part of RCU’s efforts to empower farmers, stimulate agricultural production and enhance the economic value of local crops, supporting the sustainability of the agricultural sector and contributing to the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030.
    -- SPA
